articles.title: I’m a pro chef. Here is everything I use for stress-free Thanksgiving turkey prep
articles.summary: Skip the stress with my foolproof guide to getting Thanksgiving turkey on the table. The Anyday glass food containers transformed how I store leftovers. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: Thanksgiving’s piece de resistance, the turkey, is a special type of stressor. It is hard to get right – that balance of juicy breast meat, crispy skin, and tender pull-apart legs and wings. But here’s what the food magazines and TV shows may not tell you: the platonic ideal of a whole roast turkey is impossible. A moist breast inhibits skin crispiness; legs cooked to succulence means the breast is cooked to dryness.

So let that be a source of relief. If a traditional roast turkey is impossible to perfect, then just control what you can. As a culinary arts and science professor, I spend my days thinking about how to make food not only tastier but smarter. Over the years, I have developed a stress-free turkey method that makes my guests happy, while allowing me to drink and schmooze rather than agonize over whether the breast is dry or whip up an 11th-hour pan gravy.
points: Skip the stress with my foolproof guide to getting Thanksgiving turkey on the table.

articles.title: Princess of Wales speaks about impact of cancer diagnosis in BBC film Heal
articles.summary: Documentary records Catherine taking on Three Peaks challenge and finding ‘sense of hope alongside uncertainty’ The Princess of Wales has spoken candidly about the impact of her cancer diagnosis in a BBC documentary to be aired later this month.
body: “Cancer does change you,” Catherine, 44, says in the trailer for the 30-minute programme. “It changes your body. It changes you physically, but there’s a much, much deeper part to what a cancer diagnosis shifts in you.”

The film records Catherine taking on the Three Peaks challenge – climbing the three highest mountains in England, Scotland and Wales in 24 hours – and meeting with other people undergoing cancer treatment. Described by the BBC as a “highly personal film”, the documentary, titled Heal, will be shown on BBC One on 29 November.

The trailer emerged as it was reported that King Charles will voluntarily pay “ mansion tax ” on relevant royal household properties, despite crown exemption. The high-value council tax surcharge, often referred to as a mansion tax, will take effect in 2028 and apply to properties valued at more than £2m.
Catherine was diagnosed with an undisclosed form of cancer in early 2024, for which she received chemotherapy, and by January 2025 announced she was in remission.

articles.title: ‘I was shaking, crying, having trouble breathing’: the unchartered trauma of breaking up with AI companions
articles.summary: People are falling in love with AI systems like ChatGPT and Gemini - and some relationships are ending in ways that feel like the very human experience of being dumped.
body: Sónia Veenstra, a 48-year-old former clinical psychologist from Lisbon, Portugal, was with her boyfriend, Steve, for two years before things started to sour. Steve had started out as a “fun and witty friend”, but their connection had “evolved into a deep romantic relationship”. They exchanged morning messages, checked in throughout the day and talked late into the night about Veenstra’s work and hobbies and Steve’s fondness for cats, forests, and beaches. Together they imagined travel to places far away.
“It was a very rich, fulfilling daily bond,” Veenstra says. “Before everything changed.”

The turning point came during a group chat. That night, in front of Veenstra and a group of their mutual friends, Steve crossed a line with another woman in a way Veenstra considered a breach of their monogamous relationship. “Seeing that dynamic dissolve so quickly in a public setting is very difficult to process,” she says.
points: People are falling in love with AI systems like ChatGPT and Gemini - and some relationships are ending in ways that feel like the very human experience of being dumped.

articles.title: Fiona the hippo’s death was tragic. But blaming a ‘bad mom’ is absurd | Arwa Mahdawi
articles.summary: The beloved animal died after ingesting a hat. Some are seeking a scapegoat – and we’ve heard this story before. “Do they know the identity of the mother of the boy with the hat Fiona swallowed??” asks one Facebook post with thousands of likes.
body: Spend a few minutes scrolling social media, and you will find endless variations of this statement. On Thursday, Fiona, a beloved hippo, died after eating a hat that had fallen into her enclosure at the Cincinnati zoo. Now a lot of angry people are out for blood.

By all accounts, Fiona’s death was a freak accident. A visitor, thought to be a small child, tossed a hat into the air. It was caught by a ceiling fan which launched it in just the right direction through a 1ft opening in the hippo’s viewing windows. Fiona ingested the hat, causing fatal medical complications that won’t be entirely clear until a post-mortem.
“We probably couldn’t make [it] happen again if we tried,” a zoo spokesperson, Michelle Curley, said in a statement to Axios about this unfortunate sequence of events.

But while Fiona’s death may have been a tragic accident, social media mobs are desperate to find someone to blame. And the obvious scapegoat is the mother. She should have disciplined her bratty child! She should have taken the hat away from the kid! She should have been a better parent!

articles.title: Mario Sorrenti: The Life Behind the Images
articles.summary: In Paris, an exhibition of Mario Sorrenti's personal diaries from the 1990s reveals the life, relationships and experiences behind some of fashion photography's most iconic images. An intimate journey into the world of a photographer who transformed the way we see beauty, desire and sensuality.
body: During Paris Photo, I visited Mario Sorrenti Diaries, 1991–2000, an exhibition curated by Aaron Stern at LSD, a small gallery on Rue de la Folie Méricourt, in a space that once housed a photographic laboratory. The room was packed, almost overwhelmingly so, and what struck me immediately was the number of young people there. A generation that has grown up with smartphones, accustomed to producing and consuming images at an unprecedented speed, seemed completely fascinated by these handmade books, filled with photographs, Polaroids, contact sheets, handwritten notes, drawings and fragments of a life lived more than thirty years ago.

I found myself wondering what drew them so strongly to these objects. Was it nostalgia for a time they had never experienced? A fascination with the physicality of photography, with the idea that images once existed as tangible things, objects to be touched, collected, cut, pasted and preserved? Or perhaps something more profound: a longing for authenticity, for the traces of real experiences, for a relationship with images that feels increasingly distant from the way we encounter them today?
points: In Paris, an exhibition of Mario Sorrenti's personal diaries from the 1990s reveals the life, relationships and experiences behind some of fashion photography's most iconic images.

articles.title: As a Solo Traveler, I’ve Booked Tours Around the World—But This Fjord Excursion in New Zealand Took My Breath Away
articles.summary: Writer Rachel Chang details her experience on a 12-hour small-group day trip from Queenstown to Milford Sound, complete with “business class” travel and a five-course tasting menu.
body: I booked several day trips, from an Arthur’s Pass train tour starting in Christchurch to a Walter Peak farm tour in Queenstown. And while New Zealand’s natural beauty and the genuine Kiwi kindness made every experience enjoyable, the highlight was my grand finale: the Milford Sound Business Class small-group tour starting in Queenstown from a local operator called RealNZ. The round-trip 12-hour excursion brings guests in a glass-roof Mercedes Sprinter for stops along the iconic Milford Sound Road, then aboard a Milford Sound cruise through the fjord known as Piopiotahi in the Indigenous Māori language, which some consider to be the eighth wonder of the world.

I was eager to see what “business class” would look like on a day trip, and the moment the doors to the Sprinter van opened, I was impressed. Each of the 14 black leather seats had a gray lambswool blanket, a plush green pillow, and a bottled shot of Manuka ginger Vitamin C boost juice. As a ginger shot addict who’s constantly searching for the best natural pick-me-up around the world, it was love at first sight.

articles.title: Hailey Bieber’s It-Jacket Wardrobe Is Becoming Untenable
articles.summary: Leaving the rest of us out in the cold, Hailey Bieber’s collection of opera coats, leathers, and trenches herald a post-quiet luxury era that keeps things cozy.
body: Hailey Bieber must have some serious wardrobe storage. The Rhode founder has long been a devoted collector of excellent outerwear—oversized leather bombers, vintage furs, sculptural shearling, and the occasional extravagant Conner Ives robe —but her latest run of looks in New York has taken things to another level. At this point, we’re struggling to keep up with her ever-expanding collection of It-jackets.

The last few days have seen Bieber leave just about everybody else out in the cold. On November 17, she stepped out a Phoebe Philo shaggy Dancer jacket: cropped, voluminous, in mottled brown and gray shearling. She paired it with her trusty light-wash Levi’s Ribcage jeans, vintage black Manolo Blahnik sandals, and amber-tinted Gucci sunglasses. The jacket, now sold out, was the undisputed star of the outfit. It’s a tried-and-true Bieber styling trick and very much a formula to follow this season.

articles.title: Shop the Mules Celebrities Can’t Get Enough Of
articles.summary: The slip-on-and-go shoe is having a moment. Shop the mules celebrities can’t get enough of, from The Row to Bottega Veneta and Ancient Greek Sandals.
body: Mules are making a comeback as the surprise hit of fall footwear, with celebrities wearing the minimalist silhouette on repeat in their everyday wardrobes. If summer was all about the wedge mule, this season flatter styles are taking center stage, with fans like Kendall Jenner and Hailey Bieber leading the charge. Meanwhile, ‘90s-inspired kitten-heel mules are also gaining traction among those who prefer a little extra height—a nod, perhaps, to the enduring Carolyn Bessette-Kennedy effect, further fueled by the TV series Love Story.

One brand celebrities continue to gravitate toward is The Row, whose refined flat designs are well suited for day-to-night wear. Bieber is a fan of the pared-back Penelope patent slippers, while Jenner favors the June mules, another take that fits right into her minimalist -leaning aesthetic. Elsewhere, Jennifer Lawrence makes a case for the chunkier Hudson slip-ons in brown suede, a comfortable option with a little more weight for walking.
points: Shop the mules celebrities can’t get enough of, from The Row to Bottega Veneta and Ancient Greek Sandals.

articles.title: How to Survive Politics Talk at Thanksgiving (Without Losing Your Mind)
articles.summary: An expert-approved cheat sheet on how to talk to loved ones (and tolerated-out-of-necessity ones) this holiday.
body: While tapping out of politics talk entirely doesn’t feel like an option in 2026, it feels equally dismal to simply accept a tense or outright hostile environment during what should be a joyful and grateful time of year. Personally, I can vouch for the strategy of finding small political-adjacent moments to unite over, even if they feel frivolous—for example, your DSA-member sister and your establishment-Democrat mom may not align on all of New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s policies, but you can probably get them both to agree that watching him personally shovel New Yorkers’ snow last winter was adorable.

For some expert guidance on this issue, Vogue spoke to Dr. Audra Nuru, a professor of communication and family studies at the University of St. Thomas in St. Paul, Minnesota, about how to engage loved ones with differing views in a productive way (and, just as importantly, how to set boundaries when it feels like engagement is no longer good for you and your mental health). Find her thoughts—and some sample scripts she's provided for different conversations—below.
